title: Nine Years of Asking
subtitle: 职员与店员 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 职员与店员（社会服务与人际沟通·职业与岗位）
meta: 主题语境：职员与店员（社会服务与人际沟通·职业与岗位）　|　核心词汇：clerk　|　正文 337 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 clerk 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1952 my mother was sent to ask ① clerk she could not pay, and she said the asking was the whole of the lesson. The ② clerk, meaning the person and not the counter, was nine years in the shop and was asked by whoever came last; clerk, she said, is the only thing in an office that is judged by how much has been taken out of it.

Every ③ clerk in that office had the same pen, and the ④ clerk at the end, meaning the one the manager kept and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever asked properly. Clerk, my grandmother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to stay behind; my mother said the patience is the part that gets everywhere.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ clerk was the whole of the ledger, meaning the record it carried and not the person. The ⑥ clerk, meaning the record and not any of that, is the only thing in a ledger that everybody signs and nobody questions; clerk, he said, is either something you ask or the only word that means both a person and a record. She said the record is the part they remember.

By 1967 the ⑦ clerk had become a number in a report, and the report had become an argument about the pen. The ⑧ clerk of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was nine years and eleven years of asking; clerk, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to stand on a chair. He said the chair was never mentioned.

The ⑨ clerk I remember is the one at the end, which was asked in 1972 and is still described as the oldest in the county. A ⑩ clerk, my grandmother said in 1977, is the only thing that improves by being asked; every clerk, she said, is a record that has agreed to look like a person. She said the record was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 职员（指那个人本身，与那个柜台相对）
C. 固定搭配：ask a clerk 询问一位职员
D. n. 职员（指那间办公室里每一位）
E. n. 职员（指末尾那一位）
F. n. 账目（抽象：它记下的那笔记录）
G. n. 那笔记录（抽象：那件事本身）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: The clerk, meaning the person and not the counter
clerk was the whole of the ledger
the clerk had become a number in a report
The clerk of the whole thing
A clerk, my grandmother said in 1977

answers.why: ask a clerk 意为“询问一位职员”，1952 年母亲被派去询问她付不起工钱的那位职员。
clerk 意为“职员、店员”，指那个人本身而不是那个柜台，在店里干了九年，由最后来的人询问。
clerk 指那间办公室里每一位职员，每一位都是同样的钢笔。
clerk 指末尾那一位（经理留下的那一位），是唯一有人认真询问过的。
clerk 意为“账目”，抽象指它记下的那笔记录，父亲说 clerk 就是那本账簿的全部。
clerk 为抽象用法，指那笔记录本身，是一本账簿里人人都签字、却没人质疑的东西。
clerk 意为“职员、店员”，到 1967 年这位 clerk 成了报告里的一个数字。
clerk 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是九年与十一年的询问。
clerk 意为“职员”，我记得的是末尾那一位，1972 年询问过，至今仍被说成全县最年长的。
clerk 为抽象总称，祖母说一位职员是唯一会因为被认真询问而变好的东西。
